Compute how well each node is predicted by the network

Source: R/predictability.R
net_predict.Rd

net_predict() computes the predictability of each node in a network. The predictability of a node is the proportion of its variance explained by the nodes it is connected to (Haslbeck & Waldorp, 2018): where centrality describes how a node is connected, predictability describes how much of the node's variation its connections account for. It places the edges on an absolute scale: a node with low predictability depends largely on variables outside the network, which limits how far it can be changed through its neighbours.

For Gaussian graphical models, predictability is the explained variance (R^2), which follows from the estimated precision matrix without the data. For a relative-importance network (relimp_network()) it is the R^2 stored with the fit. For the nodewise models (ising_fit(), ising_sampler() and mgm_fit()) it is computed from the data by predicting each node from the others: R^2 for continuous nodes and, for binary nodes, the proportion of correct classifications (CC) and the normalized accuracy (nCC), the gain over always predicting the more frequent category as a share of the gain that was possible.

It returns one row per node, with the type of the node, the metric used and its value, and the raw accuracy of binary nodes.

node_predictability() returns the same values as a vector for plotting; net_boot() with predictability = TRUE gives bootstrap intervals for Gaussian graphical models.

Usage

net_predict(x, data = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted network (psychnet), or a psychnet_group (one table per group).

data

The data the network was estimated from; required for the nodewise models (ising, ising_sampler, mgm), ignored otherwise.

...

Unused.

Value

A data frame with one row per node and columns node, type ("gaussian" or "binary"), metric ("R2" or "nCC"), predictability (the value of metric) and accuracy (CC for binary nodes, NA for Gaussian ones). For a psychnet_group, one table per group (see psychnet_result_group).

Details

For a Gaussian graphical model with precision matrix \(\Theta\) and correlation matrix \(S\), the predictability of node \(j\) is \(R^2_j = 1 - 1 / (\Theta_{jj} S_{jj})\).

For the nodewise models, the columns of data are matched to the nodes by name (the original column names, then the node labels) when the names allow it, and otherwise by position; binary categories are coded as when the network was fitted, and a category not seen in fitting is refused. Incomplete rows are left out.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input for a network without predictability (for example from cor_network() or tmfg_network()); for a nodewise model when data is missing, lacks columns for some nodes, contains a category not seen in fitting, or has no complete row; for a mixed graphical model with a categorical node of more than two levels; and for a group of within- and between-person networks.

References

Haslbeck, J. M. B., & Waldorp, L. J. (2018). How well do network models predict observations? On the importance of predictability in network models. Behavior Research Methods, 50(2), 853-861. doi:10.3758/s13428-017-0910-x

See also

node_predictability(); net_centralities() for centrality; net_boot() for intervals.

Examples

S <- 0.4^abs(outer(1:6, 1:6, "-"))
net_predict(ebic_glasso(cor_matrix = S, n = 250))
#>   node     type metric predictability accuracy
#> 1   V1 gaussian     R2      0.1568160       NA
#> 2   V2 gaussian     R2      0.2711166       NA
#> 3   V3 gaussian     R2      0.2711166       NA
#> 4   V4 gaussian     R2      0.2711166       NA
#> 5   V5 gaussian     R2      0.2711166       NA
#> 6   V6 gaussian     R2      0.1568160       NA
# Nodewise models need the data they were fitted to.
b <- dichotomize(SRL_GPT)
net_predict(ising_fit(b), data = b)
#>   node   type metric predictability  accuracy
#> 1  CSU binary    nCC      0.7744361 0.9000000
#> 2   IV binary    nCC      0.7769784 0.8966667
#> 3   SE binary    nCC      0.6641791 0.8500000
#> 4   SR binary    nCC      0.7173913 0.8700000
#> 5   TA binary    nCC      0.0000000 0.5000000
